title: The specified compact-support quotient tower has a normalized coherent realization
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c_0=(j_0,p_0)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $F_n=Rf^{c_0}_{!,n}=Rp_{0*,n}j_{0!}$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].

For $T=X,Y$ put $B_{T,n}=(A_n)_T$ and $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n B_{T,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$ for restriction along $B_{T,m}\to B_{T,n}$ and $\operatorname{Res}_n$ for restriction along $\widehat R_T\to B_{T,n}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}B_{X,n}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Assume there are integers $a\leq b$ such that every $K_n$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], let $\rho_{m,n}:K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$ be induced by the quotient map $P\otimes B_{X,m}\to P\otimes B_{X,n}$. Its adjoint $\beta_{m,n}:K_m\otimes^L_{B_{X,m}}B_{X,n}\to K_n$ is the canonical iterated-reduction isomorphism. These maps are independent of the representative, have identity units, and satisfy the quotient cocycle for $r\geq m\geq n$.

Put $M_n=F_nK_n$ and let
$$\tau_{m,n}:M_m\xrightarrow{F_m(\rho_{m,n})}F_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}F_nK_n$$
use the specified compact-support restriction-of-scalars comparison in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Then $(M_n,\tau_{m,n})$ is a normalized DVR tower in the full sense of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. More explicitly, $\tau_{n,n}=1$ and $\tau_{r,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}(\tau_{m,n})\circ\tau_{r,m}$, and the tensor/restriction adjoint of $\tau_{m,n}$ is precisely
$$M_m\otimes^L_{B_{Y,m}}B_{Y,n}\longrightarrow F_n(K_m\otimes^L_{B_{X,m}}B_{X,n})\xrightarrow{F_n(\beta_{m,n})}M_n,$$
where the first arrow is the canonical compact-support tensor comparison; both arrows are isomorphisms. There exist cochain complexes $C_n$ of $B_{Y,n}$-module sheaves, identifications $[C_n]\cong M_n$ in their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and chain maps $C_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}C_n$ representing $\tau_{n+1,n}$. Their composites represent every $\tau_{m,n}$. After restriction to $\widehat R_Y$ these form a strict inverse sequence of complexes, hence a coherent realization $\mathcal M_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_{\widehat R_Y}(Y))$ with precisely the evaluations and transitions required by [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Its adjacent transitions are those specifying the integral compact-support limit in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

proof.text: Choose a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] its tensor reductions compute every $K_n$ independently of this choice. Apply [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] to $\widehat R_X\to B_{X,m}\to B_{X,n}$: its balancing isomorphism is $\beta_{m,n}$, represented by $(x\otimes u)\otimes v\mapsto x\otimes q_{m,n}(u)v$. The representative-normalized adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] identifies the quotient map with $\rho_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(\beta_{m,n})\eta_{m,n,K_m}$. Indeed both send $x\otimes u$ to $x\otimes q_{m,n}(u)$. Naturality of the balancing isomorphism and the adjunction makes this independent of $P$. Identity quotients act identically; the two composites for $r\ge m\ge n$ both send $x\otimes u$ to $x\otimes q_{r,n}(u)$, proving the input cocycle.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); input normalization for blueprint Proof paragraph 2

proof.text: Write $\sigma_{m,n}:F_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}F_n$ for [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars], with the fixed compactification $c_0$ throughout. Define $\tau_{m,n}=\sigma_{m,n,K_n}F_m(\rho_{m,n})$, as in the statement. Expand $\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}(\tau_{m,n})\tau_{r,m}$. Naturality of $\sigma_{r,m}$ moves $F_m(\rho_{m,n})$ past $\sigma_{r,m,K_m}$; the resulting expression is $(\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}\sigma_{m,n,K_n})\sigma_{r,m,\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n}F_r(\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}\rho_{m,n}\circ\rho_{r,m})$. The comparison-composition clause of the cited lemma and Step 1 identify this with $\sigma_{r,n,K_n}F_r(\rho_{r,n})=\tau_{r,n}$. For identity coefficients its open comparison is the identity on underlying extension-by-zero sheaves, and its proper comparison is the inverse of the identity resolution map, so $\sigma_{n,n}=1$ and $\tau_{n,n}=1$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, the coefficient maps make a normalized tower; explicit quotient cocycle

proof.text:
Put $L_T=-\otimes^L_{B_{T,m}}B_{T,n}$ and let $\eta_T$ be its scalar unit. Let $\gamma:L_YF_m\to F_nL_X$ be the canonical tensor comparison of [def-coef-compact-support-tensor-comparison]. Its defining equation is $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(\gamma_{K_m})\eta_{Y,F_mK_m}=\sigma_{m,n,L_XK_m}F_m(\eta_{X,K_m})$. Naturality of $\sigma$ at $\beta_{m,n}:L_XK_m\to K_n$ therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(F_n\beta_{m,n}\circ\gamma_{K_m})\eta_{Y,M_m}=\sigma_{m,n,K_n}F_m(\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(\beta_{m,n})\eta_{X,K_m})=\tau_{m,n}.$$
By the bijection of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], the displayed composite is precisely the adjoint of the specified transition, not merely an isomorphism with the same endpoints.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, identify the actual coefficient maps with the specified tensor/restriction adjoints

proof.text: Every $K_m$ and $K_n$ is intrinsically bounded constructible by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. The ordinary derived $n$-reduction of $K_m$ is $K_n$ by Step 1, hence is bounded constructible too. Apply [lem-finite-compact-support-scalar-comparison] with its upper level equal to our $m$, its lower level equal to our $n$, ground field $k$, and compactification $c_0$. Its conclusion is invertibility of exactly the scalar-unit/restriction adjunct defining $\gamma$, so $\gamma_{K_m}$ is an isomorphism. Also $F_n(\beta_{m,n})$ is an isomorphism because $\beta_{m,n}$ is one. Thus the adjoints in Step 3 are isomorphisms. All hypotheses hold: $\ell\ne p$ makes $\ell$ invertible in $k$, the schemes are finite type, and $f$ is separated finite type. The assumed Tor interval also gives the finite-Tor input required in the blueprint's coefficient-change formulation; no flatness of $A_n$ over $A_m$ is used.

proof.text: Construct representatives inductively, using [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]. Choose a complex $C_1$ representing $M_1$. Suppose $i_n:[C_n]\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n$ has been chosen. Choose any $B_{Y,n+1}$-complex $D$ representing $M_{n+1}$, with $d:[D]\xrightarrow{\sim}M_{n+1}$. In $D(B_{Y,n+1})$ consider $(\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}i_n)^{-1}\tau_{n+1,n}d:[D]\to[\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}C_n]$. The cited calculus represents it by a roof $D\xleftarrow{s}C_{n+1}\xrightarrow{t_n}\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}C_n$ in the homotopy category, with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. Choose chain-map representatives of $s,t_n$ and put $i_{n+1}=d[s]$. Then $(\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}i_n)[t_n]=\tau_{n+1,n}i_{n+1}$. This induction never changes an earlier $C_n$, and every $C_{n+1}$ remains a complex over $B_{Y,n+1}$. The maps $t_n$ give the required adjacent transitions; induction on $m-n$ using Step 2 shows their composites represent every $\tau_{m,n}$.

source.place: Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic), both calculi of fractions; explicit sequential roof induction supplying the coherent-realization requirement

proof.text: Restrict $C_n$ to $\widehat R_Y$ and restrict $t_n$ along $\widehat R_Y\to B_{Y,n+1}$. Scalar restriction is termwise and leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $q_{n+1,n}\pi_{n+1}=\pi_n$, so the targets are exactly $\operatorname{Res}_n C_n$. Define the map from level $m$ to $n$ as the finite composite of the adjacent maps; associativity gives a strict inverse sequence. In cochain degree $r$ take the tower $(\operatorname{Res}_n C_n^r)_n$, with differential $(d_{C_n}^r)_n$. Each $t_n$ is a chain map, so this differential is a tower morphism, and its square is zero levelwise. Localizing this complex of towers gives $\mathcal M_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_{\widehat R_Y}(Y))$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its evaluations and transitions are precisely those proved in Step 5. Together with Steps 2--4 this is every datum of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Finally, the adjacent maps coincide term for term with the transition formula of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], since both use $F_{n+1}(\rho_{n+1,n})$ followed by the same $\sigma_{n+1,n}$.

tool_uses.why: Existence of a K-flat flat-term input representative, needed to interpret all quotient maps on one model; no unit-local lemma replaces general resolution existence.

Balanced scalar reassociation and scalar-unit normalization for the input reduction cocycle; this is the general coefficient tool explicitly recommended in the parent review.
The actual derived scalar-unit adjunction identifies the specified transition with its tensor adjunct; no assertion about compact support is taken from this tool.
The fixed-compactification restriction comparison and its composition law define the very transitions under consideration.
